questions.history: Supply nodes through each bean form, with no `spring.data.redis.cluster.*` property.
questions.prediction: The PR reports plain `ClientOptions` on the parent. The merge should expose `ClusterClientOptions` with a 30-second topology refresh period in both cases.
questions.basis: Two pinned regressions assert the option type and duration. The cluster identity and requested interval are identical in the two fixtures.
questions.refutation: The connection factory uses cluster mode but returns plain options, or exposes a different period for either bean.

questions.history: Move the same nodes into `spring.data.redis.cluster.nodes` and keep the period unchanged.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should expose cluster options and the requested 30-second period.
questions.basis: The property-driven case already satisfied the parent’s test for cluster-specific configuration.
questions.refutation: A property-configured cluster loses the duration or returns standalone options.

questions.history: With a live three-node cluster supplied through connection details, shorten the period to one second. Open and initialize the client, record a quiet node’s topology-command counter after startup, then observe during an idle interval spanning several periods with adaptive triggers disabled.
questions.prediction: On the merge periodic refresh should be enabled and the cluster should see additional topology requests while idle. Allow timing and command counts to vary with the client version.
questions.basis: A node-side observation exercises the consumer of the settings. The PR author reports the counter stayed flat on the parent and rose from 7 to 13 over six seconds after the change on Redis 8.6.2.
questions.refutation: The factory exposes the requested option but the initialized client has periodic refresh off or issues no later topology request under the controlled conditions.
